scope_note: Assessments use the 2025 certified non-ad valorem roll (bills mailed Nov 2025 for FY2025-26). Utility rates and officeholders are the most current found as of 2026-10-20. Salaries: EDR statutory figures for FY2025-26 and FY2026-27.

assessments.area: Countywide developed parcels (roll does not identify city vs unincorporated; FAQ does not limit it to unincorporated)
assessments.name: Stormwater utility fee - residential (levy code STWR)
assessments.how_charged: Flat $40 per developed residential parcel; each condominium unit is a separate residential property; DOR land use 1,2,4,5,50. Exempt: qualified senior, disabled veteran and disabled-person homesteads, community cemeteries.
assessments.fiscal_year: FY2025-26 (2025 roll); rate in place since 2006 roll

assessments.name: Stormwater utility fee - commercial (levy code STWC)
MSTU - Fire Services (ad valorem, NOT a non-ad valorem assessment)
assessments.how_charged: Ad valorem millage on taxable value: 1.3800 mills for FY2026. Listed here because unincorporated fire is funded by millage, not a per-unit assessment; no county fire NAV appears on the 2025 NAV roll.

assessments.name: Street lighting assessments (levy codes ALSL1 and BOCA)
assessments.how_charged: Flat per parcel within each lighting unit (ALSL1 $60.00 x 43 parcels; BOCA $27.00 x 33 parcels). DOR county total for Lighting = $3,471. Unit names not decoded from public listing.

assessments.government: Bay County (Board of County Commissioners) - per DOR classification
assessments.name: Levy code PPCD (DOR function: community development/redevelopment)
assessments.how_charged: Parcel-specific amounts ($1,003.38 to $199,609.02); total $1,013,419.22. Code likely refers to the Pier Park Community Development District (Panama City Beach) - NOT confirmed; DOR files it under the county.

assessments.name: Liens / other (levy codes LIEN, PCN)
assessments.how_charged: Parcel-specific; LIEN 241 parcels $312,691.90; PCN 17 parcels $22,155.28. DOR county 'Other' total $334,847.

assessments.name: Fire service assessment (levy code PCF)
assessments.how_charged: By property type: homesteaded residential dwelling unit $150 (maximum); non-homestead residential (e.g., rentals) $300 per unit; vacant land $24.51 per parcel (FY2024-25 figure, matches 2025 roll); commercial/non-residential by building square footage and fire-response factors (per-sq-ft rates not found).
assessments.rate: $150 homestead unit / $300 non-homestead unit / $24.51 vacant parcel

assessments.name: Fire service assessment (levy code PBF)
assessments.how_charged: Two tiers: Tier 1 per $1,000 of improvement value (Property Appraiser) + Tier 2 flat per tax parcel. Noticed MAXIMUM FY2025-26 rates: $0.78 per $1,000 improvement value + $95.66 per parcel (4% over FY2024-25).
assessments.residential_note: Depends on improvement value. Median billed per parcel on 2025 roll = $348.68 (all parcel types).
assessments.caveat: Amounts on the 2025 certified roll do not reconcile exactly with the noticed maximum rates: the smallest non-zero PBF bill is $103.17 (1,068 parcels billed $103.17 fire and $56.70 stormwater), and fire/stormwater Tier-1 amounts on the roll move in a 1.531 ratio rather than the 0.78/0.49 = 1.592 ratio. The adopted final rate resolution was not located.

assessments.name: Stormwater management assessment (levy code PBSW)
assessments.how_charged: Tier 1 per $1,000 improvement value + Tier 2 per parcel. Noticed MAXIMUM FY2025-26: $0.49 per $1,000 improvement value + $48.30 per parcel.
assessments.residential_note: Depends on improvement value. Median billed per parcel on 2025 roll = $217.10 (all parcel types).
assessments.caveat: See PBF caveat; smallest non-zero PBSW bill on roll is $56.70.

assessments.area: Front Beach Road Community Redevelopment Area only
assessments.name: Front Beach Road CRA assessment (levy code PBCRA)
assessments.how_charged: Category A $38.95 per parcel flat; Category B weighted: $0.009 per heated/AC sq ft (60%), $0.04 per $1,000 improvement value (30%), $0.06 per $1,000 land value (10%). Noticed maximum FY2025-26.
assessments.rate: $38.95 per parcel (Category A) or weighted by building size and value (Category B)
assessments.residential_note: Median billed per parcel on 2025 roll = $75.13.

assessments.name: Stormwater assessment (levy code LN)
assessments.how_charged: Per equivalent billing unit (1 unit = 3,900 sq ft impervious area); vacant land 0.28 units. Adopted Aug 2021 at about $139 per unit. FY2025-26 per-unit rate not found; FY2026 budget carries $2,652,000 non-ad valorem stormwater revenue.
assessments.rate: about $139 per unit (2021 adoption); current per-unit rate not located

assessments.name: Fire assessment (levy code SF)
assessments.how_charged: Not documented in a located resolution. 2025 roll: most common bill $146.57 (721 parcels); median $207.40; amounts vary by parcel.

assessments.government: City of Callaway / City of Springfield
assessments.name: Other (levy codes CN - Callaway, SN - Springfield; likely liens)
assessments.how_charged: Parcel-specific: CN 3 parcels $24,315.34; SN 2 parcels $14,079.83 (DOR municipal 'Other' total $38,395).

assessments.government: Lake Powell Residential Golf Community Development District (independent special district)
assessments.area: Wild Heron, unincorporated Bay County (about 724 acres)
assessments.name: CDD assessments (levy code LPWH1)
assessments.how_charged: Per-lot CDD assessment; 2025 roll 560 parcels, median $2,219.01, range $1,674.32-$28,428.27.
assessments.caveat: Code-to-district match (LPWH = Lake Powell / Wild Heron) is an inference from the name.

assessments.name: Levy code SB (DOR function: community development)

assessments.government: Independent special districts (unidentified, codes PW, WMH)
assessments.name: Lighting assessments (DOR function: lighting)
assessments.how_charged: Flat per parcel: PW $141.00; WMH $92.00. DOR ISD lighting total $9,290.

utility_rates.area: Bay County retail water/wastewater service area (unincorporated customers where the county is the retail provider)
utility_rates.garbage_note: County Solid Waste Division does not provide collection; it runs the Steelfield Road landfill (disposal only).
utility_rates.stormwater_note: County stormwater is a $40/yr non-ad valorem charge on the tax bill, not on the utility bill.
utility_rates.calc: Water: 21.10 + 3 x 2.60 + 2 x 2.90 = 34.70; Sewer: 37.00 + 5 x 9.80 = 86.00; Total = 120.70 (3/4-inch meter, 2026 column; assumes wastewater volume charge on all metered water)
utility_rates.effective: Fee schedule header 'Effective April 21, 2026'; uses the '2026' column (prior '2025' column took effect Jan 1, 2025)

utility_rates.provider: City of Panama City Utilities (water, wastewater, garbage)
utility_rates.area: Panama City (city utility also serves parts of unincorporated Bay County)
utility_rates.stormwater_note: No stormwater line listed in the rate notice.
utility_rates.calc_caveat: The city's FAQ says the average residential bill becomes 'approximately $92.29', which equals the three base charges alone - so usage may include an allowance not described in the notice. Treat the 5,000-gallon figure as provisional until the rate ordinance is checked.
utility_rates.effective: October 2026 usage (first bills week of Nov 2, 2026)

utility_rates.provider: City of Panama City Beach Utilities
utility_rates.garbage_note: Not on the city rate sheet; not located.
utility_rates.stormwater_note: Stormwater is a non-ad valorem assessment on the tax bill (PBSW), not on the utility bill.
utility_rates.calc: 5,000 gal is within the 6,000-gal minimum: water 37.54 + sewer 49.88 = 87.42 (rate sheet also shows combined 0-6,000 gal water+sewer = 87.42)
utility_rates.calc_caveat: Sheet says billing is bi-monthly on even months while headings say 'monthly ... per unit'; figure is per month as labeled.

utility_rates.stormwater_note: Stormwater is a non-ad valorem assessment on the tax bill (LN).
utility_rates.effective: FY2025-26 rates as printed in budget approved Sept 23, 2025 (FY2026-27 budget exists but could not be downloaded; rates may have changed Oct 1, 2026)

utility_rates.provider: City of Callaway Utility Billing (water/sewer purchased wholesale from Bay County)
utility_rates.calc: Water 11.37 + 5 x 5.32 = 37.97; franchise fee 10% = 3.80; Sewer 30.69 + 5 x 6.13 = 61.34; Stormwater 1.00; Solid waste 13.00; Total = 117.11
utility_rates.calc_caveat: The city's rates page mislabels its headings (outside-city base rates appear under 'per 1,000 gallons'); figures were matched by the stated 25% outside surcharge (11.37 x 1.25 = 14.21; 30.69 x 1.25 = 38.36; 5.32 x 1.25 = 6.65; 6.13 x 1.25 = 7.66). FY2027 budget assumes consumption rates rise $0.05 (water) and $0.15 (sewer) to cover county increases, which may not yet be on the page.

utility_rates.provider: City of Springfield Public Works / Utility Billing
City of Mexico Beach (water/wastewater supplied by Bay County; city bills)
utility_rates.calc: Water 40.83 + 1 x 3.68 = 44.51; utility tax 7% = 3.12; Sewer 55.07 + 1 x 5.20 = 60.27; Sanitation 40.00; Total = 147.90 (city's stated minimum bill is $138.76)
utility_rates.effective: Not stated ('current monthly rates', page retrieved 2026-10-20); council raised water 2.6% and sewer 4% on Oct 28, 2025

utility_rates.calc: Not computed - no published rate schedule located. FY2025-26 draft budget shows a 10% city utility tax on water and garbage 'permit fees' (suggesting private haulers).

notes: Levy-code list comes from the Florida DOR NAV D file for Bay County (county 13), 2025 roll: 21 levy codes, 128,201 parcel-levy lines. DOR government type 1=county, 2=municipality, 3=independent special district. Code-to-name matches marked as inferred are not confirmed by a public code table.

The Tax Collector's NAV page lists only assessment types (paving, stormwater, solid waste); it does not publish a list of levying authorities. baycountyfltax.gov and baypa.net returned HTTP 403 to automated requests.

Unincorporated Bay County fire service is funded by the 1.38-mill MSTU (ad valorem), not a per-unit fire assessment. City fire assessments exist only in Panama City (PCF), Panama City Beach (PBF) and Springfield (SF).
Bay County stormwater ($40 residential / $200 commercial) appears on 42,113 + 1,530 parcels; the roll does not show which are inside cities.

No solid waste/garbage non-ad valorem assessment is on the 2025 Bay County roll. Garbage is billed monthly on city utility bills (Panama City $45.91, Springfield $37.67, Mexico Beach $40.00, Lynn Haven $24.86, Callaway $13.00).
EDR salary figures are the Chapter 145 statutory formula amounts; EDR says they apply to elected officers and should be verified by each county. FY2026-27 uses April 1, 2025 population estimates.
City elected-official pay is shown only as combined budget lines where per-member amounts were not published; dividing those lines would be an estimate and was not done.

Bay County commission page and county directory disagree on chair: the directory lists Doug Moore as Chairman; the commission page lists Clair Pease as Chairman and Daniel Raffield as Vice Chairman. WJHG reported Moore stepped down as chairman on Nov 18, 2025, which supports the commission page.
Panama City Beach's noticed FY2025-26 fire and stormwater rates are maximums; the 2025 roll amounts do not reconcile exactly with them (see caveat on PBF).
gaps: Final adopted rate resolutions not located for Panama City fire (commercial per-square-foot rates), Panama City Beach fire/stormwater/CRA (only the maximum-rate notice found), Lynn Haven stormwater (current per-unit rate), and Springfield fire (rate method).

Several levy codes could not be matched to a named district: SB, PW, WMH, TWIN, ALSL1, BOCA, OERR, PCN; PPCD (probably Pier Park CDD) and LPWH1 (probably Lake Powell Residential Golf CDD) are inferred.

Typical single-family amounts for value-based assessments (PCB fire/stormwater, Lynn Haven stormwater, Springfield fire) can't be stated without parcel-level property-use data. The DOR NAL parcel file for 2025 wasn't available from the portal, so only all-parcel medians are given.
Parker: no published water/sewer/garbage rate schedule found, and no FTE count.
Panama City Beach: no residential garbage rate and no employee count (the budget book couldn't be downloaded).
Panama City: the 5,000-gallon bill is provisional, because the city's 'average bill' equals its base charges alone. No stormwater fee found.
Lynn Haven: the FY2026-27 budget (which may carry rates effective Oct 1, 2026) could not be downloaded because the connection was reset; FY2025-26 rates are used.
Callaway: the rates page shows no effective date, and the FY2027 budget assumes small consumption increases that may not be on the page yet.
Mexico Beach and Springfield: no FTE counts found. Springfield and Parker have no city manager; a City Clerk handles administration.

Manager salaries not found: Bay County (Joel Schubert), Panama City (Jonathan Hayes; only his requested $175,000 minimum was reported), Lynn Haven (Chris Lightfoot), Mexico Beach (Mell Smigielski). The Panama City Beach figure is the 2021 contract base. Department-head salaries were not compiled.

School board: the full current member roster with districts and term ends wasn't verified (the district website doesn't render it). Superintendent McQueen's 2024 election status and term end weren't verified.
Lynn Haven, Springfield and Parker seat term-end dates are not published on their sites.
Bay County commissioner term ends were derived from election cycles (2024 FAC results, 2026 qualifying list), not from a single county roster.
